title: Query-Preserving Security for Traditional Cycle Walking
summary: Reverse 2-cycle walking achieves the broader domain-restriction goal, but proving traditional cycle walking secure without amplifying reduction queries remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Let $S=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ and $T=\{0,\ldots,2N-1\}$, and let $E_{\mathrm{part}}$ be a block cipher on $T$ whose security is assumed only against $N$ queries. Determine whether traditional cycle walking can produce a cipher $E_{\mathrm{full}}$ on $S$ with security against $N$ adversarial queries while admitting a reduction that makes at most $N$ queries to $E_{\mathrm{part}}$. The unresolved obstacle is query amplification: each query to $E_{\mathrm{full}}$ may require many queries to $E_{\mathrm{part}}$, potentially forcing the reduction to query nearly all $2N$ points of $T$ and thereby exceed $E_{\mathrm{part}}$'s assumed security threshold.

scope.domain: Finite-domain block-cipher security reductions for traditional cycle walking.
assumptions: The block cipher E_part on T is assumed secure only against N queries.
parameters: N: determines the N-point target domain S, the 2N-point source domain T, and the stated query bounds
E_part and E_full: the underlying cipher on T and the desired traditional-cycle-walking cipher on S
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether traditional cycle walking can achieve N-query security on S through a reduction making at most N queries to E_part despite query amplification.

citations.label: Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications

progress.summary: The source presents traditional cycle walking as a possible approach but identifies query amplification as the barrier to a security reduction. It proves the larger transformation with reverse 2-cycle walking rather than resolving that barrier for the traditional method.
citation_labels: Sarah Miracle et al., Reverse Cycle Walking and Its Applications
